extracted.intended_audience: Citizens/voters of New York and the American public considering ratification of the proposed Constitution (late 1787)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing the adequacy and design of a federal constitution, focusing on powers, enforcement, representation, finance, defense, and judicial authority. Derived from Hamilton/Publius arguments in the Federalist Papers (Nos. 20–23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'sovereignty over sovereigns' (no government over governments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sovereignty over sovereigns, a government over governments, or legislation for communities as opposed to individuals is a theoretical solecism and in practice subversive of civil polity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create an authority whose exercise substitutes naked violence for lawful coercion by magistracy; constitutional design should operate through law applied to individuals/objects, not by assuming supremacy over other sovereign entities in a way that encourages coercion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution must provide an enforceable SANCTION to its laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal constitution must include explicit power to exact obedience and punish disobedience (pecuniary mulcts, suspension/divestiture of privileges, or other constitutional modes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of delegated authority to enforce resolutions renders national laws dead letters. A written provision leaving enforcement to inference creates absurdities and undermines the Union. Anti-pattern: relying on only moral suasion or tacit powers without express enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual guaranty of State governments against violent usurpation
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal plan should include a guaranty by the national government to protect State governments from usurpation or violent overthrow; such guaranty is not an improper interference in lawful reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guaranty should be narrow in scope (operate against violent, not legal, changes) and should enable aid to repel domestic dangers that threaten State constitutions. Anti-pattern: assuming utility implies an implied guaranty in violation of express delegation clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: National government must be authorized to raise its own revenues (avoid quotas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulating State contributions by fixed QUOTAS or requisitions is fundamentally unequal and inadequate; the national government should be authorized to raise revenue directly (imposts, excises, duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas based on land value or population produce glaring inequality because no common measure of wealth exists. Prefer national imposts/excises which more flexibly distribute burdens across citizens and can self-limit by affecting consumption levels. Anti-pattern: relying on requisitions that cannot be enforced and produce inequality/oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer indirect taxes (imposts/excises) as a chief revenue source
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties on articles of consumption are self-regulating: if set too high they reduce consumption and defeat the revenue aim; thus they naturally limit excess and reduce risk of material oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indirect taxes as primary revenue in a new nation; they equilibrate over time and avoid the uniform, odious operation of quotas. Example: imposts and excises will, in time, find their level with citizens' ability to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: If direct taxes are used, prefer apportionment by population (numbers) for simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct taxes (land/building related) may admit apportionment rules, and population numbers are preferable to land valuations because land valuation is costly, difficult, and impracticable in a growing country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a fixed, ascertainable rule (population) over a complex valuation of land to reduce administrative burden and expense. Anti-pattern: attempting detailed land valuations in an imperfectly settled country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal power to regulate commerce is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: A power to regulate commerce (with other nations and among the States) is necessary to form beneficial treaties and prevent interstate conflicts and clashing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without federal superintendence, separate State regulations frustrate treaties, invite foreign advantage-taking, and can treat citizens of other States as aliens, impeding internal and external trade. Anti-pattern: leaving commerce regulation to individual States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal authority must have clear powers to raise, govern, and support armed forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities essential to common defense include raising armies, building/equipping fleets, prescribing rules for their government, directing operations, and providing for their support; these powers should exist without limitation due to unpredictable national exigencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the extent and variety of national dangers are infinite, constitutional constraints that prevent adequate defense are imprudent. Anti-pattern: relying on requisitions of men by States (quotas) which cause costly bounties, short enlistments, fluctuating troops, and discipline failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on quotas and requisitions for troops or funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that require States to supply quotas of men or money produce competition, excessive bounties, short terms of service, inefficiency, unequal burden distribution, and are an imbecility in union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorize national methods for recruiting and funding forces to ensure economy, stability, and fairness. Example of failure: auction-like competition for men during the recent war; anti-pattern: expecting delinquent States to make retrospective compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not give equal suffrage among States primacy over representation by population
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal suffrage between States of widely unequal population contradicts the republican maxim that the sense of the majority should prevail and risks injustice, minority domination, and eventual revolt by larger States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation and voting rules should reflect proportion or otherwise provide practical mechanisms to avoid small-state vetoes over majority interests. Anti-pattern: granting Rhode Island, Delaware equal weight with populous states in national deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid high supermajority or unanimity requirements that enable minority obstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring concurrence of a large number (near unanimity) allows a minority to obstruct necessary governmental action, invites foreign corruption (easier to bribe fewer actors), and hampers timely responses in crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design decision rules so that majority or appropriately-weighted majorities can act, reducing risk of paralysis. Example: two-thirds requirements make corruption or foreign intrigue easier than a simple-majority rule; anti-pattern: institutionalizing a small minority's ability to veto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a single supreme judiciary to give laws and treaties effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws and treaties are dead letters without courts to expound and define them; a supreme tribunal under the authority that makes treaties is indispensable to produce uniformity in determinations and prevent contradictory final decisions across States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a national court of final jurisdiction to avoid divergent state-court rulings, local bias, and undermining of general laws. Anti-pattern: leaving each State as court of final jurisdiction for national laws and treaties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Found national authority on the consent of the people (popular ratification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fabric of national government ought to rest on the consent of the people rather than mere ratification by state legislatures, which leaves open arguments about repeal and the validity of delegated powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use popular ratification to deepen legitimacy and prevent doctrines that a party to a compact (state legislature) may revoke the compact; anti-pattern: resting national foundations solely on legislative ratifications susceptible to repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper organization of the national legislature for expanded powers
rubrics_metrics.description: A single assembly is an inappropriate repository for enlarged powers required by a national government; organization and distribution of authority must match the nature and extent of powers to be exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Union is to be entrusted with substantial powers, the legislative organization should be structured (bicameralism, checks, distribution) so as to prevent accumulation of prerogatives in a single, unstructured body and to protect against potential tyranny arising from concentration of power.
